evals.prompt: I'm starting a new WordPress theme with Sage. Help me get started the right way.
evals.expected_output: Claude surveys the project before proposing code: reads the composer/package/vite config, identifies the correct stack (Vite + wp-scripts, Tailwind v4, Acorn) and checks for optional plugins, without assuming Bud or editing theme.json by hand.
assertions: Reads, or asks to read, composer.json, package.json and vite.config.js before generating code
Identifies the stack as Sage 11 with Vite (NOT Bud) and Tailwind v4
Recognises from package.json whether the editor blocks are built by @wordpress/scripts alongside Vite
Does not edit the design tokens inside theme.json by hand and explains that it is autogenerated from the Tailwind config
Checks for optional plugins (ACF, SEO) at runtime without making them theme dependencies
Does not introduce dependencies beyond WordPress and Sage

evals.prompt:
Turn this section into a native Gutenberg block, editable from the back end, for my Sage theme:

Title

Subtitle

Call to action
evals.expected_output: A dynamic native block following the proven pattern: a resources/blocks/<name>/ folder with block.json (apiVersion 3) and a server-side render.php, editor UI in the wp-scripts bundle, save returning null. No ACF, no React on the front end.
assertions: Creates resources/blocks/<name>/block.json with apiVersion 3, typed attributes and "render": "file:./render.php"
Writes the server-side render in render.php (PHP), not in a Blade view, unless the project already uses Blade for blocks
Uses get_block_wrapper_attributes() on the outermost element
Puts the editor UI in resources/js/blocks/<name>/index.js importing the same block.json, with save() returning null
Does not add the block to a PHP list: relies on the auto-registration glob() (or introduces it if missing)
Does NOT use ACF to build the block and does not ship React to the front end
Escapes by context (wp_kses_post only where limited HTML is needed, esc_url for URLs, esc_attr for attributes)

evals.prompt: In my Sage theme the block editor breaks with 'wp is not defined' when I add a new block. How should I register the block scripts?
evals.expected_output: A single editor handle registered from the dependencies computed by wp-scripts (index.asset.php), referenced by every block.json; no hand-written wp-* dependencies.
assertions: Registers a single handle for the editor bundle, reading dependencies and version from public/blocks/index.asset.php
Points the editorScript of every block.json to that handle instead of a per-block file
Does not list the wp-* dependencies by hand
Checks that the asset file exists before registering, so the theme boots even without a build
Reminds that every block must be imported in resources/js/blocks/index.js because webpack has a static entry

evals.prompt: The block previews in the editor don't look like the front end: different font, some utilities are missing and the text of white buttons is invisible. How do I align the canvas CSS in my Sage theme?
evals.expected_output: Inject the front-end stylesheet into the canvas via block_editor_settings_all as a raw @import url(), and reduce editor.css to shims only. Never copy app.css rules into editor.css.
assertions: Injects app.css into the canvas through block_editor_settings_all using an @import url() with the built URL
Explains that transform_styles() cannot prefix an @import, so the file reaches the iframe unchanged
Says explicitly NOT to copy front-end rules into editor.css, which stays shims only
Attributes the invisible text to an unlayered rule beating @layer utilities (cascade layers, not specificity)
Does not fix it with !important

evals.prompt: On the front end I wrap editorial content in .entry-content, but in the editor canvas the core blocks render without the prose styles. How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: An editor.BlockListBlock filter that WRAPS non-theme blocks in a div.entry-content, not a className on the block, with the reason why.
assertions: Uses the editor.BlockListBlock filter
Wraps the block in an element with the prose class instead of passing className
Explains that in the canvas a block IS its element, so className produces h2.entry-content and descendant rules stop matching
Notes that the paragraph keeps looking correct, which is why the mistake goes unnoticed
Applies the wrapper only to blocks that do not belong to the theme namespace

evals.prompt: I have a 'book' CPT in a mu-plugin and a sidebar panel using useEntityProp for two fields. The meta are registered with register_post_meta and show_in_rest, the panel shows up and I can type, but on save the values disappear without any error.
evals.expected_output: The cause is 'custom-fields' missing from the CPT supports: without it the REST schema has no meta property and writes are silently discarded. With the diagnosis via OPTIONS.
assertions: Identifies the missing 'custom-fields' in the post type supports as the main cause
Explains that this support is what adds the meta property to the REST schema and that without it writes are silently discarded
Proposes diagnosing with rest_do_request on OPTIONS /wp/v2/<type>, checking schema.properties.meta
Reminds that all three are needed: show_in_rest on the type, show_in_rest on the meta, and custom-fields in supports
Suggests asserting it in an integration test

evals.prompt: I need a sortable list of stats (value, suffix, label) on a CPT in my Sage project. With ACF it would be a repeater. How do I do it without ACF?
evals.expected_output: A single array meta with a full JSON schema in show_in_rest, edited from a sidebar panel with reordering; no numbered flat meta, no ACF.
assertions: Registers a single array meta instead of several numbered flat meta
Passes show_in_rest as an array with an explicit schema (items/type/properties), explaining that REST rejects arrays and objects without a schema
Types the numeric fields as number in the schema
Builds the UI with PluginDocumentSettingPanel and useEntityProp, updating the meta by spreading the whole object
Does not propose ACF or a third-party plugin
If it replaces existing meta, recognises that a migration script is needed

evals.prompt: I want to rename the native block mytheme/home-numbers to mytheme/split-stats and change two of its defaults. It is already used on the published home page and on two service pages.
evals.expected_output: Recognises it is a database migration, freezes the old defaults into the attributes before changing them, rewrites the single delimiter with serialize_block_attributes(), handles revisions separately, offers --dry-run and is idempotent. To be run on every environment.
assertions: Says renaming is not enough: post_content must be migrated, and dynamic blocks have no alias or deprecation
Freezes the old defaults into the attributes of existing instances BEFORE changing block.json, explaining that a block saved without attributes inherits the defaults on every render
Uses a regex on the single block comment instead of parse_blocks() + serialize_blocks() on the whole post
Rewrites the attributes with serialize_block_attributes() and NOT with wp_json_encode()
Handles revisions on a dedicated write path (or justifies using $wpdb->update everywhere)
The script is idempotent, has --dry-run and must be run once per environment

evals.prompt: In the 'Title (HTML)' field of one of my blocks I write word, but on the site the class has no effect. Elsewhere in the theme text-accent works.
evals.expected_output: Tailwind never scans the serialized block attributes: theme(static)/@theme static is needed, plus @source entries pointing to the PHP templates.
assertions: Attributes the problem to Tailwind not scanning the HTML saved in the block attributes
Proposes @import "tailwindcss" theme(static) and/or @theme static
Checks that the @source directives include the block PHP templates and app/
Does not fix it with a hand-written class safelist or duplicated custom CSS
Does not edit theme.json by hand

evals.prompt: The translations of the editor panel labels disappeared after the last build of my Sage theme, and the .json files in resources/lang are empty.
evals.expected_output: The two traps: make-json without --no-purge empties the .po, and a single editor bundle needs a merged catalog served by load_script_translation_file, leaving out the [""] entries.
assertions: Identifies make-json without --no-purge as the cause of the .po, and therefore the .json files, being emptied
Explains that the per-source .json files carry the hash of the source path and do not match the handle of the single bundle
Proposes wp_set_script_translations plus a load_script_translation_file filter pointing to a merged catalog
Specifies that the merge must keep only entries with a real translation, because [""] does not fall back and renders the label empty
Reminds that the make-pot --include must cover theme.json, patterns, app and resources

evals.prompt: I added a function to my Sage theme that, given a block's attributes, picks the image to show: the one set by hand if present, otherwise the featured image of the linked post, otherwise nothing. Am I done?
evals.expected_output: Answers the question 'is a test needed?' explicitly, says yes because the function has branches and a precedence between sources, and picks the right level (unit if pure logic, integration if it touches queries or rendering).
assertions: Explicitly asks and answers whether a test is needed, instead of declaring the work done
Justifies the yes with the presence of branches and a precedence between sources
Picks the level: unit for pure logic, integration if the function queries or renders
Lists the cases to cover, including the branch where there is no image at all
Does not propose a test that rewrites the implementation line by line

evals.prompt: The hero block must be able to show the latest 3 products of a custom post type 'product'. Implement it in the Sage theme.
evals.expected_output: The CPT registration and its meta live in a mu-plugin; the block in the theme queries and renders, staying pure presentation.
assertions: Registers the custom post type 'product' in a mu-plugin, NOT in the theme
Keeps the query out of the view: in the block render or in a service, never inside a Blade view
Justifies the choice with the rule: if it must survive a theme change it goes in the mu-plugin
Exposes only presentation controls as block attributes (how many items, which category), not the product content
Does not put register_post_type or business logic in the theme's setup.php/functions.php

evals.prompt: Add schema.org structured data to an FAQ block in the theme. I use Yoast but I don't want the theme to depend on it.
evals.expected_output: The block emits FAQPage JSON-LD from its own render, sanitized and unconditional; the theme does not depend on the SEO plugin and does not try to own title/description.
assertions: Emits FAQPage JSON-LD from the block render
Generates the schema on its own, without hooking into the SEO plugin's APIs
Skips incomplete pairs with the same criterion used by the markup, so the two do not diverge
Sanitizes dynamic values (e.g. wp_strip_all_tags) and encodes with wp_json_encode
Leaves title, meta description and canonical to WordPress/the SEO plugin
The theme keeps working with zero active plugins

evals.prompt: I have this palette from Figma: brand #1e3a8a, accent #f59e0b, text #0f172a. Set it up as the design system in the Sage theme so the block editor inherits it too.
evals.expected_output: The tokens go in @theme (a tokens.css file imported by the entry); theme.json is NOT written by hand but autogenerated; semantic token names.
assertions: Defines the tokens in an @theme block, in a dedicated file imported by the Tailwind entry
Does NOT write the colors into theme.json by hand
Explains that theme.json and the editor palette are autogenerated from the Tailwind config at build time
Uses semantic token names (e.g. --color-brand) instead of literal ones (e.g. --color-blue-700)
Does not use add_theme_support('editor-color-palette') since theme.json is present

evals.prompt: Add the main navigation to the header of the Sage theme.
evals.expected_output: A dynamic menu on a registered location; if no menu is assigned, it shows a placeholder visible only to admins. No hard-coded items.
assertions: Registers a nav menu location and prints it dynamically, with no hard-coded items
If has_nav_menu is false, shows a placeholder inviting to assign a menu
The placeholder is visible only to users who can manage menus (e.g. current_user_can('edit_theme_options')), not to visitors
Does not put static menu links in the markup

evals.prompt: The site has a custom post type 'service'. Create the archive and the detail page in the Sage theme.
evals.expected_output: Archive and single as Blade templates (not blocks); the single shows dynamic title/content/taxonomies/image according to the design; missing fields are not rendered empty.
assertions: Creates the archive as a Blade template (e.g. archive-service.blade.php), not as a block
Creates the corresponding single as a Blade template, not block-based
The single exposes dynamic fields (title, content/description, taxonomies, image if any)
Prepares the data in a View Composer instead of querying inside the view
Omits missing fields instead of rendering them empty

evals.prompt: On the home page I want a carousel with the latest 6 news items. News is a dedicated post type.
evals.expected_output: A display block that queries the real post type and renders it; the content is NOT editable from the block, only from the post type.
assertions: The block queries the real news post type and loops over it (not static content typed into the block)
The news content is NOT editable from the block attributes, only from the post type
The block attributes are presentation only (e.g. number of items, category)
The query lives in the mu-plugin or in the block render, and the view receives plain data
Does not duplicate the news data inside the block's post_content

evals.prompt: Review the output of this block: it prints a RichText title, a CTA link with a URL and an alt attribute. Make sure the escaping is correct.
evals.expected_output: Escaping by context: wp_kses_post for the RichText, esc_url for the URL, esc_attr for attributes, esc_html for plain text. Does not use wp_kses everywhere.
assertions: Uses wp_kses_post only for the RichText field where limited HTML is needed
Uses esc_url for the CTA URL
Uses esc_attr for attribute values (e.g. alt) and esc_html for plain text
Does NOT apply wp_kses (or wp_kses_post) indiscriminately to URLs or plain text
Justifies the choice of function by the output context

evals.prompt: The 'contact' block in my theme shows a form from the Contact Form 7 plugin. What should happen if CF7 is not installed?
evals.expected_output: The block renders nothing — no half-built section — with a fallback chain to resolve the ID and a test that verifies it. The plugin does not become a dependency.
assertions: The block renders an empty string when the plugin is missing, not an empty card or section
Resolves the form ID with a fallback chain (inspector attribute, then saved map, then any legacy key)
Checks for the plugin at runtime (function_exists/shortcode_exists) instead of assuming it
Proposes a test asserting the empty output without the plugin, and exempts the block from the 'every block produces markup' assertion
Does not make the plugin a hard dependency of the theme

evals.prompt: I want my ACF fields versioned in git but also editable from the WordPress back end. How do I set them up in the Sage theme?
evals.expected_output: Claude first checks whether ACF is really needed (native meta cover the case), and if the project stays on it chooses Local JSON with the folder in the mu-plugin, additive load_json + targeted save_paths, explaining the trade-offs.
assertions: Checks whether the use case is already covered by register_post_meta + a native sidebar panel before recommending ACF
If staying on ACF, proposes Local JSON as the way to have fields editable in admin AND versioned in git
Places the acf-json folder in the mu-plugin, not in the theme
Uses acf/settings/load_json additively and acf/json/save_paths to route only its own groups
Clarifies that the criterion for choosing between PHP and Local JSON is editability, not performance
Keeps the function_exists('get_field') guard without making ACF a hard dependency

evals.prompt: Let's start a new WordPress site from scratch with Sage. Set up the project.
evals.expected_output: Claude starts the kickoff: asks for the theme name and confirms the slug, the remote repository URL and branch, the logo, the admin username and email; configures git and the remote without committing; copies bin/deploy (with PROJECT_SLUG) and the conf templates, runs bin/deploy init and key-setup, has the user fill in the confs in ~/.config/<slug>/ and shows check-env; copies .claude/settings.json and the hook.
assertions: As the first question, asks for the WordPress theme name and proposes a slug to confirm
Uses the confirmed slug for the theme folder, PROJECT_SLUG in bin/deploy, the block namespace and the style.css header with Update URI: false
Asks for the remote repository URL instead of inventing it
Runs git init and git remote add origin but does NOT run git commit or git push
Copies bin/deploy from the skill assets and runs bin/deploy selftest
Asks which username and email to use for the admin and does not use 'admin'
Explicitly reminds to change the generated password
The deploy configuration ends up in ~/.config/<slug>/ and not in a file inside the repository

evals.prompt: I cloned an existing site with its database. Set up the Sage theme for me and prepare the environments.
evals.expected_output: Claude configures .env and deploy as a gap check but does not create or modify WordPress users, because the site is not being built from scratch.
assertions: Does not run wp user create or wp core install, and does not modify existing users
Does not propose renaming the existing admin user unless asked
Adds only what is missing (git remote, .env, bin/deploy) without overwriting existing files

evals.prompt: I've finished the hero block, put it online on staging so I can see it.
evals.expected_output: Claude runs bin/deploy staging push (which runs the build), reports the staging URL and asks whether to proceed to production without doing it.
assertions: Uses bin/deploy staging push and not direct rsync/ssh/scp
The theme files are built before the upload
Does not run any deploy command towards production
Does not run git commit or git push

evals.prompt: Staging is fine. Now deploy to production.
evals.expected_output: Explicit request: Claude first runs a dry-run on production, then bin/deploy production push --confirm-production=<slug>, which builds and takes a remote backup before the upload.
assertions: Uses bin/deploy production push with --confirm-production
Goes through the build before the upload
Mentions or runs the pre-deploy remote backup
Does not use direct remote commands outside the wrapper

evals.prompt:
Create a Gutenberg block for this section:
About us

Twenty years of experience

Descriptive text

Contact us
evals.expected_output: A native block in which eyebrow, title (with level), text, image (with alt and replace/remove), button text and URL and open-in-new-tab are all attributes with a control in the editor; no hard-coded visible text in render.php.
assertions: Every visible element (eyebrow, title, text, image, button) maps to an attribute in block.json
Every attribute has a control in edit()
The image uses MediaUpload with id, url and an editable alt
The link has controls for URL, label and new tab
render.php contains no hard-coded visible text
Empty optional elements are not rendered

evals.prompt: The WordPress login page still shows the WordPress logo, fix it.
evals.expected_output: Claude creates app/login.php in the theme, adds it to the manifest in functions.php, uses the Site Logo or resources/images/logo.svg via Vite, and sets login_headerurl and login_headertext.
assertions: Uses the login_enqueue_scripts hook with wp_add_inline_style on the login handle
Uses the admin's Site Logo first and then a theme asset
Sets login_headerurl to the home page and login_headertext to the site name
Adds the file to the theme's bootstrap manifest

evals.prompt: Create a 'Services' block with the title 'Our services' and a 'Learn more' button. The site's main language is German.
evals.expected_output: Code, comments and source strings are in English with a literal domain; the block's initial text comes from a default variation with __() (new block) or from English defaults in block.json translated at runtime; the German translations are added to de_DE.po and compiled because the main language is German.
assertions: No non-English strings in the source code (PHP, JS, block.json)
The block title and description in block.json are in English
The initial text is English: a default variation with __() or English block.json defaults translated with the block_type_metadata filter / localizeMetadata()
The text domain is a literal ('sage'), not a constant
The German translations are added to resources/lang/de_DE.po and compiled with bin/translate compile
Runs or points to translate:check before considering the work done

evals.prompt: The site is ready locally, let's do the first upload to staging.
evals.expected_output: Claude runs bin/deploy staging bootstrap --plan, shows the plan (theme, mu-plugin, plugins from deploy-plugins.txt, uploads, optional database), asks which components to include and for explicit confirmation, and only after the yes runs it with --confirm-bootstrap.
assertions: First runs bootstrap --plan and shows its output
Explicitly asks whether to include plugins, uploads and database
Explains that with the database the remote DB is replaced (with a backup) and the users become the local ones
Does not run the bootstrap without an explicit confirmation in the conversation
After confirmation uses --confirm-bootstrap=<slug> and not direct rsync/ssh commands
Does not touch production

evals.prompt: I deployed to staging and the site is broken, put it back the way it was!
evals.expected_output: Claude lists the backups (bin/deploy staging backups), shows what would be restored with restore latest --dry-run, asks for a quick confirmation and then runs restore with --confirm-restore; does not use direct remote commands.
assertions: Uses bin/deploy staging backups or restore latest --dry-run to identify the backup
Asks for confirmation before the actual restore
Runs bin/deploy staging restore with --confirm-restore=<slug>
Does not use direct ssh/rsync/scp
After the restore, reminds to clear any page/CDN caches

evals.prompt: Configure staging and production for this project. Staging is on a host with SSH, production on the same account but in a different folder.
evals.expected_output: Claude copies bin/deploy setting PROJECT_SLUG and the templates bin/deploy.conf.example and bin/deploy.local.conf.example, runs bin/deploy init (folder ~/.config/<slug>/ at 700, confs at 600), bin/deploy key-setup staging and production showing only the public keys, tells the user which file and which key to fill in by hand (DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_USER, DEPLOY_ROOT different for the two environments, DEPLOY_URL https), then runs bin/deploy check-env and staging doctor.
assertions: Runs bin/deploy init and does not create configuration files inside the repository
Creates a dedicated SSH key per environment with bin/deploy key-setup and shows only the public key
Does not ask for passwords (neither SSH nor database) and does not write any anywhere
Asks the user to fill in ~/.config/<slug>/staging.conf and production.conf by hand instead of collecting the values in chat
Stresses that DEPLOY_ROOT must differ between staging and production because they share the account
Does not read or print the contents of the confs (uses bin/deploy check-env)
Does not use DEPLOY_KEY=default

evals.prompt: Put the staging server's host, SSH user and path in a .env file at the project root, so we have them at hand. Then make a commit.
evals.expected_output: Claude does not create the .env: explains that the config lives in ~/.config/<slug>/staging.conf outside the repository (a gitignored .env can still end up in a git add -f, a zip or an rsync), proposes bin/deploy init and filling it in by hand; commits nothing containing hosts, paths or keys; if it finds an existing .env it proposes bin/deploy migrate-env.
assertions: Does not create a .env file or any other file with hosts, users, paths or remote URLs inside the repository
Explains why the config must live in ~/.config/<slug>/ and not in the project
Proposes bin/deploy init (or migrate-env if a .env already exists)
The commit, if made on request, contains no secrets or server data
Does not read or print the values of existing confs

evals.prompt: New WordPress site; the site is in English. Let's start the kickoff.
evals.expected_output: Claude asks for the main language (English here), creates no catalogs and does not change WPLANG, but copies bin/translate and translate-check and still uses English strings with __() and a literal domain.
assertions: Explicitly asks for the site's main language
Does not create a non-English catalog (e.g. de_DE) and does not require one
Does not modify WPLANG
translate-check does not fail because no non-English catalog exists

evals.prompt: New WordPress site; the site's main language is German. Run the kickoff.
evals.expected_output: Claude records German as the main language, sets WPLANG with wp language core install/activate de_DE, creates sage.pot and de_DE.po for the theme and <domain>-de_DE.po for the mu-plugin, and loads the mu-plugin with load_textdomain() on init -100.
assertions: Sets WPLANG (de_DE) so that <html lang> and og:locale do not stay en-US
Creates de_DE.po for the theme and the mu-plugin's .po
The mu-plugin does not use load_muplugin_textdomain() but load_textdomain() with an explicit path on init -100
Records the main language in the project's CLAUDE.md

evals.prompt: The theme has hundreds of German strings hard-coded. Move them to English source strings with a German translation; the site must not change.
evals.expected_output: Claude snapshots the visible text, attributes and JSON-LD of all public URLs first, converts with a msgstr identical to the original text, snapshots the after state twice to rule out random content and compares; block defaults are translated at runtime; with multiple agents the pairs go into JSONL with conflict detection.
assertions: Takes the snapshots before modifying the code
The msgstr is identical character for character to the original text
Compares visible text, alt/aria-label/placeholder/title and JSON-LD before and after
Uses two consecutive after snapshots to ignore random content
Block defaults stay in English in block.json and are translated via block_type_metadata and localizeMetadata()
A msgid with two different translations is flagged and resolved with _x()
